implied_expectations.price_basis: US$414.00 per ADS, close 2026-09-01 (an alternative source quoted US$416.09 intraday). Not a tier-1 transacted price — the ADS price is the one input here that is not from a primary filing.

share_count.basis: FACT (tier-1, 20-F cover): 25,932,524,521 common shares outstanding at 2025-12-31

implied_expectations.source_conflict_resolved: Aggregators reported market capitalisation of both US$1.93T and US$2.15-2.16T in early September 2026. Computing from the tier-1 share count (5,186.5M ADS x US$414.00) gives US$2,147B, confirming the higher figure. The US$1.93T quote is stale or wrong. Per policy/source-policy.yaml the conflict is shown and the preferred source explained rather than silently picked.
implied_expectations.net_cash_derivation: FACT (tier-1): cash, cash equivalents and current marketable securities NT$3,068,595M (US$97,820M) at 2025-12-31; short-term loans NIL; aggregate long-term debt NT$1,032,988M (US$32,929M).

three_year_margin_trajectory_pct.why_this_is_the_central_fact: Margins EXPANDED while revenue grew 76% cumulatively over two years. That is the signature of a strengthening competitive position, not of a cyclical rent. It is the single clearest differentiator versus 005930, whose margin surge came from a +220% memory ASP spike.

capex.focus: 2nm and 3nm capacity (Fabs 20, 21, 22), specialty and advanced packaging (Fab 24), and R&D
capex.self_funding: 2025 capex of NT$1,272,411M against only NT$86,900M of bond issuance — roughly 93% funded from operating cash flow.

dividends.note: No share repurchases. Capital return is dividend-only, so there is essentially no income floor under the position.

current_year_trading.company_guidance: FY2026 revenue growth slightly above +40% YoY in USD terms
current_year_trading.forward_visibility: 2nm capacity booked well into 2028; CoWoS sold out through the 2026 ramp from roughly 75-80k to 120-130k wafers per month.

multiples.forward_estimate_basis: ESTIMATE: FY2026 revenue near US$170B (+40% on FY2025's US$121.4B, per company guidance) at a 47% net margin gives roughly US$80B of net income, or US$15.42 per ADS.
multiples.sensitivity: HONEST LIMITATION — the forward multiple rests on the analyst's own margin assumption. TSMC does not guide margin. At FY2025's 44.6% net margin instead, FY2026 net income is roughly US$76B, EPS US$14.65 and the forward P/E 28.3x.

reverse_engineered_requirement.method: Solve for the net income that justifies US$2,147B at a range of mature multiples, then compare with the FY2026 estimated base.
reverse_engineered_requirement.at_20x: requires roughly US$107B of net income — about 34% above the FY2026 estimate
reverse_engineered_requirement.at_25x: requires roughly US$86B — approximately the FY2026 estimated level
reverse_engineered_requirement.at_30x: requires roughly US$72B — below the FY2026 estimate
reverse_engineered_requirement.conclusion: At a 25x mature multiple the price requires the FY2026 estimated earnings level to PERSIST, not to grow. That is a positive expectation gap, and the visibility behind it is unusually good — 2nm booked into 2028 and CoWoS sold out. The gap is nonetheless thin, and it is thinner than it looks on trailing numbers (39.7x).

bear.narrative: AI capex digests and leading-edge utilisation falls. At 33% capex intensity the fixed-cost base bites hard and margins normalise toward the 2023-24 range. Node migration continues but pricing power moderates. NO Taiwan event.
bear.note: Milder than either the 005930 or NVDA bear, because there is no rent to lose and no off-balance-sheet commitment to strand.

base.narrative: AI and node migration keep compounding. TSMC retains the leading-edge monopoly, advanced-node mix keeps rising, and margins hold near current levels as overseas fab dilution offsets scale gains.

bull.narrative: Leading-edge demand exceeds capacity through the decade. A16 and successors extend the lead, advanced packaging becomes a second profit pool with its own pricing power, and TSMC captures more of the value it enables.

permanent_loss_case.definition: Permanent impairment of more than 70% of capital, not a drawdown.
permanent_loss_case.primary_scenario: A Taiwan contingency. The overwhelming majority of capacity — nine Hsinchu fabs, two Central Taiwan, seven Southern Taiwan, plus Fab 22 Kaohsiung — sits on one island, on leased science-park land. Overseas capacity (Arizona, Kumamoto, Dresden, Washington) is material but not a substitute at leading edge.
permanent_loss_case.secondary_scenario: A decisive process-technology loss to Intel 18A or Samsung SF2 combined with the 33%-of-revenue capex base becoming stranded. Judged far less likely than the geopolitical case on current evidence.
permanent_loss_case.why_this_differs_from_the_other_names: 005930's bear is a cycle; NVDA's is a demand pause. Both are drawdowns against solvent businesses. TSMC's tail is a genuine loss of the asset base, and it is UNHEDGEABLE and UNRESEARCHABLE — no amount of analysis converts it into a measurement.
permanent_loss_case.confidence_in_this_estimate: LOW (0.40) — deliberately stated as a judgement, not a measurement.

subjective_probabilities.labelled: EXPLICITLY SUBJECTIVE. The Taiwan contingency is modelled as a SEPARATE tail rather than folded into the bear case, because its mechanism and severity are categorically different.
subjective_probabilities.sensitivity_warning: Most sensitive to the Taiwan contingency weight, which is the least knowable input in this file. At 0.10 instead of 0.05 the weighted return falls to roughly +32%; at 0.02 it rises to roughly +41%. The verdict does not flip across that range — which is itself informative, and is why the position is sized rather than rejected.

notes: Step order per agents/valuation.md: reverse expectations first, then scenarios, then asymmetry, then score. No target price used as a starting point. Every financial input is tier-1 from the 2025 Form 20-F; the ADS price is the sole non-primary input. The FY2026 forward estimate rests on the analyst's own margin assumption and is labelled ESTIMATE throughout. The asymmetry score of 4 is LOWER than NVDA's 5 despite TSMC having the better business — a high probability of a good-but-bounded outcome plus a small probability of near-total loss is a worse outcome shape than a wider band with no catastrophic tail.
